fieldValues.title: D3. Place: the level and boundary where a decision removes choices
fieldValues.thinking_reached: The ideal: every decision names the level and boundary (domain) where it removes choices; shown elsewhere it is context, not a decision. What we have: no decision in the programme log records its domain or level (0 of 109); 14 are design-kind, technical choices in the strategy log, e.g. 01cfb06e typed ErrorReport details (srs-rust#1342). Boundaries exist as types (com.mudemocracy.argument boundary, narrows), domains as method records, but decisions are not placed on them.
fieldValues.tensions: Define domains first, and sense them from where decisions land. The owner: do not move the problem to domain definition; sense where domains are needed and keep watching; domains may merge from experience (vignette 5f271974).
fieldValues.unresolved_questions: Which boundaries do decisions keep naming that no domain holds yet? When does a recurring boundary become a domain, and when do two domains merge?
fieldValues.next_action: Each decision placed records its boundary (a domain link, or a boundary: tag where no domain exists yet); a boundary tag that keeps recurring goes to affirmation review as a candidate domain.
